svg.text: An OpenAI-compatible API in front of an agent runtime. Hexagonal: domain (pure rules) -> application (the turn engine) -> adapters (HTTP, Postgres, Redis, MCP, the model).
OpenAI's request shape, plus a few headers
model = an agent id (or agent:upstream-model , or any upstream model)
messages = the WHOLE history -- the client is stateless; the gateway is not told a thread id
Authorization: Bearer agw_... -> who the user is
X-Agent-Skills-Env-<VAR>: ... -> this call's Jira / Confluence / GitLab credentials
tools[] and a system prompt -> the client's OWN tools and instructions
Any other model name (and every other /v1/* route) is forwarded to the
upstream unchanged, after the same key check: the gateway is a drop-in
front for the model endpoint, with agents added on top
hash the key, find the user
application/turn.py, run as a LangGraph graph: every decision is in the nodes, the graph only fixes their order
run_turn: take a Redis lock on user + history hash, then run the nodes until stage = END
last message a tool result or an
a catalog failure never fails the turn
build the toolset for THIS call:
gateway tools the user has creds for,
empty reply -> correct it, up to 4 times
more than 25 steps -> the turn fails
for each tool call the model made:
client tool -> return it to the client
client opt-in) under the new hash
a PAUSE ends here too: the response
client tool call; the rest waits
tool results go back to the model: it loops until it answers
after a pause: prepare restores the hidden work and jumps straight to dispatch
Hidden vs visible: the gateway's own tool work (reads, writes, handoffs) is kept in the PendingTurn, so the client only ever sees the visible conversation.
Corrections, not crashes: a bad tool call goes back to the model as an error message (max 4 in a row). Tool results are cut at 20,000 characters.
Writes are shown first. Handoffs reset the correction counter. The agent's own tool always replaces a client tool with the same job.
Every step is narrated in one line ("Looked up the knowledge base (5 results)", "Handing off from X to Y") through the reasoning channel.
D HOW A TURN PAUSES AND RESUMES
a write needs approval, the agent asked a question, or a client tool must run
hidden messages + remaining calls + the call, ENCRYPTED
approval expires in 15 min; other pauses in 24 h
the response ends with ONE of:
a call to the client's question tool (AskUserQuestion,
2 The code is bound to the call
an HMAC under APPROVAL_SECRET, not a free-form token
code = HMAC(user, call id, tool, hash of the arguments)
a code for one call cannot approve another, or
the same tool with different arguments
stored as a hash; compared in constant time
wrong, expired or reused -> "Nothing was changed."
the next request carries the user's answer
history hash -> the same thread (active agent, opt-in)
last message = a tool result -> take_pending(call id)
restore hidden messages and the queue, then dispatch:
approved -> run the write declined -> tell the model
a resumed turn never re-runs reads it already did
Why the thread is a hash
no thread id in the OpenAI API
history_hash = chain hash of the visible messages, per user.
Recognised by history, so a client that just replays its
messages lands on the same active agent. The hash also keys
the Redis lock: one turn at a time per conversation.
E WHO RUNS A TOOL CALL -- DECIDED PER TOOL, PER CALL
For each tool of each server the agent is bound to: does the user have the credentials it declares?
the tool is offered to the model, and any
client tool doing the same job is hidden
the agent tells the user what is missing
the tool is not offered; a client equivalent
is held back too, and `use_client_tools` is
offered instead. Only after the user says yes
does route become: client -- the client's own
connector runs it, gated by the client
F PORTS AND THE ADAPTERS BEHIND THEM
application/ports.py: what the core needs from the outside
swap an adapter by implementing its Protocol; the turn engine does not change
G DOMAIN -- PURE RULES, NO I/O
mounted read-only into the container at /etc/agent-gateway
config/agents/*.yaml -- one file, one model name
config/mcp-servers.yaml -- one entry, one tool server
client_terms (words that mark a client stand-in),
credentials: the variable NAMES it accepts -- never values
approval_ttl 900 s | pending_ttl 24 h | thread_retention 30 d
retrieval: server + tool | context windows | ask_tools styles
